review_notes: I read the whole file and the related definitions in Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Nat/Hom.lean (multiplesHom, powersHom and their simp lemmas) and Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Equiv/Basic.lean (monoidHomCongrLeftEquiv). I also read the sibling Grp/ForgetCorepresentable.lean, which uses the same pattern. A grep shows no uses of uliftMultiplesHom, uliftPowersHom or the coyonedaObjIsoForget defs outside these two files. I could not run Lean, so I did not check the exact statements that `simps!` generates. My claim about their form is inferred from the definition by composition (`Equiv.trans`) and from `monoidHomCongrLeftEquiv` being tagged `simps apply`. The finding is a moderate-confidence interface gap. The file has no looping or competing simp rules.

findings.problem: Both equivs are defined by `Equiv.trans` of `multiplesHom`/`powersHom` with `monoidHomCongrLeftEquiv`, and `@[simps!]` is used on them. The generated `_apply` and `_symm_apply` lemmas are therefore stated in terms of the composed pieces, for example `monoidHomCongrLeftEquiv` applied to `multiplesHom M x` or its `.symm`. The lemmas are unlikely to be in the canonical pointwise forms that the non-ULift versions have: `multiplesHom_apply : multiplesHom M x n = n • x` and `multiplesHom_symm_apply : (multiplesHom M).symm f = f 1`. A goal such as `uliftMultiplesHom M x ⟨n⟩` or `(uliftMultiplesHom M).symm f` has no stated simp normal form `n • x` or `f (ULift.up 1)`. The same applies to the powers version, which should give `x ^ n.down.toAdd` and `f (ULift.up (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1))`. The four `coyonedaObjIsoForget` isos have no simp lemmas either, so `(coyonedaObjIsoForget.hom.app M) f` has no stated normal form. The Grp sibling file has the same pattern.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the blanket `@[simps!]` with explicit lemmas, stated by `rfl` or a short proof. For example: `@[simp] lemma uliftMultiplesHom_apply_apply (x : M) (n : ULift ℕ) : uliftMultiplesHom M x n = n.down • x`, and `@[simp] lemma uliftMultiplesHom_symm_apply (f : ULift ℕ →+ M) : (uliftMultiplesHom M).symm f = f (ULift.up 1)`. Add the analogous `x ^ n.down.toAdd` and `f (ULift.up (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1))` lemmas for `uliftPowersHom`. Optionally add simp lemmas that `(coyonedaObjIsoForget.hom.app M)` and its inverse are given by evaluation at `ULift.up 1`. Alternatively, keep `simps!` but write `simps! apply_apply symm_apply` (or custom projections) so the generated lemmas have the pointwise form.
findings.benefit: Users can reduce expressions involving these equivalences to `n.down • x` and `f (ULift.up 1)`. This mirrors the existing `multiplesHom_apply` and `multiplesHom_symm_apply` lemmas. It avoids unfolded `monoidHomCongrLeftEquiv` and `comp` terms in simp output, and gives later code on corepresentability a stable normal form.

evidence.excerpt: @[simp] lemma multiplesHom_symm_apply (f : ℕ →+ M) : (multiplesHom M).symm f = f 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma multiplesHom_apply (x : M) (n : ℕ) : multiplesHom M x n = n • x := rfl
